# fise/ and the FISE book

`fise/` holds the MATLAB scripts behind "Foundations of Image Systems
Engineering" (FISE), a Quarto book in the sibling repository
`FISE-2025-Quarto` (not nested under this one). A script here typically
produces one of two things for the book:

- a PNG figure exported directly into the book's `chapters/images/` tree, or
- a standalone HTML tutorial page that a chapter links out to.

This skill covers only what's specific to that relationship. For how to
structure, name, run, test, or `iePublish` a script, use isetcam's
`authoring-tutorials-examples`, `publishing-tutorials-examples`,
`matlab-evaluation`, and `testing-workflow` skills — don't re-derive that
guidance here. Keep the established `fise_*` naming; it is not the same
convention as isetcam's `t_*`/`s_*`/`data_*` and should not be forced into
it.

## Chapter mapping

Subfolders under `fise/` correspond to book-chapter groups by number, not by
exact filename:

| `fise/` folder | Book chapters |
| --- | --- |
| `01Lightfields/` | `chapters/lightfields-*.qmd` |
| `02Optics/` | `chapters/optics-*.qmd` |
| `03Sensor/` | `chapters/sensors-*.qmd` |
| `04Human/` | `chapters/human-*.qmd` |
| `05Display/`, `06IP/`, `07Appendix/` | `chapters/displays-*.qmd`, `chapters/imgprocessing-*.qmd`, `chapters/appendix-*.qmd` (currently empty placeholders) |

To find which specific chapter and sentence reference a given script, search
`FISE-2025-Quarto/chapters/*.qmd` for the script's base name (e.g.
`fise_diffraction`) rather than guessing from the folder alone.

## Figure export: `fiseBookPath`

`fise/fiseBookPath.m` returns the path to the `FISE-2025-Quarto` checkout,
assumed to be at `~/Documents/FISE-2025-Quarto` (resolved via `$HOME` /
`%USERPROFILE%`, not a hardcoded absolute path), so it works across machines
with different home directories as long as the book lives at that fixed
location relative to home on each one. It errors clearly if that folder
doesn't exist rather than silently building a bad path.

This replaced `fiseRootPath`, which returned "one directory up from this
file" — correct only while this code lived at `FISE-2025-Quarto/code/`, and
wrong (pointing into `isetfise` instead) once `fise/` moved into this
repository. `fiseRootPath` is gone; every call site now uses `fiseBookPath`.

These scripts call `fullfile(fiseBookPath,'chapters','images',...)` to
export figures straight into the book:

`fise_humanMosaic.m`, `fise_humanConePSF.m`, `fise_imageHarmonics.m`,
`fise_oiAperture.m`, `fise_humanLSF.m`, `fise_lensExamples.m`,
`fise_otf2d.m`, `fise_siKernels.m`, `fise_imageHarmonics1d.m`,
`fise_opticsMTF.m`, `fise_opticsPSF.m`, `fise_otf2dFace.m`

If a new script needs to export a figure into the book, use `fiseBookPath`
the same way — never re-derive the book's location from `fise/`'s own path,
since the two repositories are independent checkouts.

## Linking a published script into a book chapter

Once a script is published with `iePublish` (inline images — see isetcam's
`publishing-tutorials-examples` skill), link to the resulting HTML from the
book chapter using `htmlpreview.github.io` against this repository's GitHub
blob URL. A raw `github.com/.../blob/...` URL shows source, not the
rendered page — it must go through htmlpreview to render.

```
https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/ISET/isetfise/blob/main/fise/<topic-folder>/<script>.html
```

Example, matching the existing chapter reference in
`optics-01b-diffraction.qmd`:

```
https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/ISET/isetfise/blob/main/fise/02Optics/fise_diffraction.html
```

The branch is `main`. Re-publish and re-check the link after any change to
the source script — htmlpreview renders whatever is currently at that blob
URL, so a stale commit shows stale output.

## Leftover artifacts from the old pipeline

Some `.html` files under `fise/02Optics/` (and their `_files`/`_media`
companion folders, e.g. `fise_opticsCountingPhotons_files/`,
`fise_opticsPSF_media/`) were carried over from the book's old
Quarto-based publishing pipeline, not generated by `iePublish`. Treat them
as stale — regenerate with `iePublish` (which produces one self-contained
file with inline images and no companion folder) rather than assuming they
reflect the current script.
